findings: The same compact representation should be compared on CPU and GPU. CPU compact already reduces eager graph/path allocation time substantially.

Warm in-process NVIDIA GPU shortest-table production has lower median graph build/query time than CPU compact; v1 first initialization costs about 2.63 seconds, so initialization and teardown must remain in lifetime accounting.

Candidate g003-r2 persistent OpenCL helper completed 27 exact table/query comparisons and 972 public-engine paths, exit 0 and no affinity violations. CPU build/query total 970.354414ms versus GPU 1007.027195ms; GPU setup+shutdown included 1322.443011ms, so this IPC design did not establish a net benefit.

A future GPU experiment should reduce result pipe copies via a shared-memory compact table, or use one persistent in-process producer with measured affinity; CPU search workers should consume a shared immutable table. Preserve CPU fallback and deadline accounting.
No solver, bridge, GPU-lab, or profile processes were observed on the three inspected PCs during read-only process checks. No matches were run by this inspection.
